cards.text: Some time later, there's a feast of the Jews, and Jesus goes up to Jerusalem. Near the Sheep Gate there's a pool called Bethesda, and on its five covered walkways lie a great number of the sick, the blind, the lame and the paralyzed. One man there has been an invalid for a long, LONG time.

cards.question: How long has this man by the pool at Bethesda been an invalid?

cards.text: Jesus sees him lying there and realizes he's spent a long time this way. So Jesus walks up and asks him a question.

cards.question: What does Jesus ask the man lying by the pool?

answers.text: Do you want to get well
Do you believe I can do this
Why are you lying out here

cards.question: You'd think the man would shout YES. Instead, he tells Jesus about a problem he has with the pool when the water is stirred. What is it?

answers.text: He has no one to help him in
The guards keep him away from it
The priests say he is unclean

cards.text: And while he's on his way, someone else goes in before him. That's circling the parking lot, spotting the open space, and watching somebody zip right into it. EVERY. TIME.

cards.question: Jesus doesn't help the man into the pool at all. What does Jesus tell him instead?

answers.text: Get up and pick up your mat and walk
Go and wash in the pool of Siloam
Go and show yourself to the priests

cards.question: After Jesus speaks, the man slowly gets better over the next few days.

cards.text: Thirty-eight years an invalid, and now he's walking around CARRYING the mat. Then comes one quiet little detail: this happened on the Sabbath day.

cards.question: The Jews see the healed man and tell him it's the Sabbath, so it's unlawful for him to ___ his mat.
The healed man answers that he's only doing what the man who made him ___ told him to do.

cards.text: So the Jews want a name: who told you to pick it up and walk? And the healed man's got NOTHING, because the best day of his life just happened and he never caught the guy's name.

cards.question: Why doesn't the healed man know who healed him?

answers.text: Jesus had slipped away in the crowd
Jesus healed him from far away
Jesus never said a word to him

cards.text: Afterward, Jesus finds the man at the temple. And Jesus has something to say to him.

cards.question: When Jesus finds the healed man at the temple, He tells him to stop sinning.
After meeting Jesus at the temple, the healed man keeps Jesus's name a secret.

cards.text: Now because Jesus is doing these things on the Sabbath, the Jews begin to persecute Him. But Jesus has an answer for them.

cards.question: When the Jews persecute Jesus over the Sabbath, how does He answer them?

answers.text: My Father is working and so am I
The Sabbath was made for man
I came to fulfill the Law

cards.question: After Jesus answers, the Jews try even harder to kill Him, and it's only because He broke the Sabbath.

cards.text: Not only was He breaking the Sabbath, He was even calling God His own Father, making Himself equal with God. And friend, Jesus does NOT back down.
So Jesus replies, and He opens with "Truly, truly, I tell you." When those words ring out, that's Mags-level loud, friend: EVERYBODY LISTEN.

cards.question: Jesus says the Son does things on His own, apart from what He sees the Father doing.
Jesus says the Father shows the Son all He does. Why?

answers.text: The Son asked to see it

cards.text: And to their amazement, Jesus says, the Father will show Him even greater works than these. Friend, a man just walked off carrying his mat after thirty-eight years, and Jesus says THAT'S not the big one.

cards.question: Just as the Father raises the dead and gives them life, Jesus says the Son gives ___ to whom He wishes.

cards.text: Then Jesus says the Father judges no one. He has assigned all judgment to the Son.

cards.question: Why has the Father given all judgment to the Son?

answers.text: So all may honor the Son like the Father
So the Father can rest from His work
So the Son can test the priests

cards.question: Jesus says whoever does not honor the Son does not honor the Father who sent Him.

cards.text: Another "Truly, truly." Now Jesus talks about whoever hears His word and believes the One who sent Him.

cards.question: Jesus says that person has eternal life and has crossed over from ___ to ___.
Jesus says an hour is coming, and has now come, when the dead will hear something. What do they hear?

answers.text: The voice of the Son of God

cards.text: Then Jesus says as the Father has life in Himself, He has granted the Son to have life in Himself. Me? I need three alarms and a warm oven just to get going in the morning.

cards.question: Jesus says the Father has given Him authority to execute judgment. Why?

answers.text: Because He is the Son of Man

cards.text: Then Jesus says, "Do not be amazed at this." Because an hour is coming for those in the graves.

cards.question: Jesus says only some of the people in their graves will hear His voice.
Those who have done good come out to the resurrection of life. Those who have done evil come out to the resurrection of ___.
Jesus says He can do nothing by Himself and that His judgment is just. Why is it just?

answers.text: He seeks the will of the One who sent Him
He has studied every law of Moses
The priests have approved His rulings

cards.text: Now Jesus says, "If I testify about Myself, My testimony is not valid." Makes sense: me saying my cookies are the best in the Dorinverse doesn't count for much when I'm the ONLY baker here.

cards.question: Jesus says there is another who testifies about Him, and that testimony is valid.

cards.text: Then Jesus brings up John the Baptist: they sent to John, and John testified to the truth. Jesus doesn't accept human testimony, but He says these things so that they may be saved.

cards.question: What picture does Jesus use to describe John the Baptist?

answers.text: A lamp that burned and gave light
A tree planted by the water
A city set on a hill

cards.question: Jesus says the people were willing to bask in John's light for good.
Jesus says He has testimony more substantial than John's. What is it?

answers.text: The works the Father gave Him to do
The crowds that follow Him around
The praise of the temple priests

cards.question: Jesus says the ___ who sent Him has Himself testified about Him.
Jesus tells them they've never heard the Father's voice or seen His form, and His word doesn't abide in them. Why doesn't it, according to Jesus?

answers.text: They do not believe the One He sent
They have never read the Law
They stopped going to the temple

cards.text: Then Jesus points to the Scriptures. They pore over them, because they presume that by them they possess eternal life.

cards.question: Jesus says the Scriptures they pore over have nothing to say about Him.

cards.text: And yet, Jesus says, they refuse to come to Him to have life. That's reading the invitation ten times, memorizing the address, and never showing up.

cards.question: Jesus says He does not accept glory from men.

cards.text: Then Jesus says He knows them, that they don't have the love of God within them. He came in His Father's name, and they have not received Him.

cards.question: Jesus came in His Father's name and they didn't receive Him. What does He say they'll do if someone else comes in his own name?

answers.text: They will ask him for a sign

cards.question: Jesus asks how they can believe when they accept ___ from one another instead of seeking it from the only God.

cards.text: Then Jesus says, "Do not think that I will accuse you before the Father." Somebody else has that job.

cards.question: Jesus says their accuser is the one they've put their hope in. Who is it?
Moses, Israel's great leader, is the one they've hoped in. Jesus says if they had believed Moses, they'd believe Him, because Moses ___ about Him.

cards.text: And Jesus ends with a question that just hangs in the air: "But since you do not believe what he wrote, how will you believe what I say?"

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 1 quotes "Truly, truly, I tell you.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 14 quotes "Do not be amazed at this.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The included sermon John 5:19-47 doesn't have a stop of its own covering exactly those verses.

rule.text: An included parable or sermon (see passages.md) gets a stop of its own.

findings.problem: The question asks why the Father shows the Son all He does and makes 'The Father loves the Son' the reason. John 5:20 says only 'The Father loves the Son and shows Him all He does.' The two clauses are joined by 'and', so the text never says the love is the reason. The card adds a reason the text doesn't give.

rule.text: Reasons: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: In John 5:31 the action is vouching for yourself, which doesn't count without another witness. The joke's point is different: his claim means little because he has no competition ('I'm the ONLY baker here'). The comparison doesn't share the core action, so it muddies the point that card 2 then asks about.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: 'I'm the ONLY baker here' contradicts his world. Papa Dorin invites bakers to come help him, and the baker reading the card is one of them. The line changes his Dorinverse story.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: The card calls him 'John the Baptist', but the passage only says 'John' (John 5:33). The card cites only John 5:33-34, so the outside fact that identifies him has no reference.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The statement 'willing to bask in John's light for good' is ambiguous. 'For good' can mean 'forever' or 'for a good purpose'. A baker who reads it the second way could argue it's true, even though the intended answer is False (John 5:35 says 'for a season').

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The wrong answers 'rich' and 'famous' don't fit the tone of a man who was just healed after thirty-eight years. 'The man who made him famous' reads as silly next to 'well', so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.
